statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ re-extended through the high that failed an hour ago and is now holding the top of the overnight band. Holding near a session extreme is one of the amplifiers this measure watches for, and it has returned. VIX settled at 15.85, the 10Y is near 4.72% and the 2Y near 4.26%, and WTI is near $85.28. Tail lifts to 13 and Stress holds at 46, which keeps the mapped state below the block threshold.

headline: NQ re-extends to a new overnight high of 29,197 and holds within 30 points of it, restoring the session-extreme amplifier on a 0.62% band; Tail lifts to 13 with Stress at 46 into Wednesday's Core PCE and Nvidia stack
body:
The observation that moves the assessment this hour is a completed re-extension. An hour ago NQ had pushed to 29,168.25 and given back roughly 55 points, and that failed extension was the reason the session-extreme amplifier cleared. Since then the contract has traded through it: Investing.com shows 29,196.25, up 90.50 points or 0.31%, and Yahoo Finance shows 29,164.75, up 59.00 points or 0.20%, on the 29,105.75 settle. The overnight band is now 29,017.00 to 29,197.00, about 180 points or 0.62%, and price is sitting in the top fifth of it. Extension, failure, then a fresh high is exactly the repeated-extension shape this measure targets, so the amplifier is back and Tail lifts from 9 to 13.

What keeps the reading inside the low band is amplitude and context. A 0.62% overnight range is unremarkable, and the grind higher has been slow rather than impulsive. Asia is repairing rather than trending in one direction: the Nikkei 225 is at 65,720.25, up 0.29%, having traded as low as 64,609.47 and as high as 65,846.19, a recovery of roughly 1.7% off the low. The KOSPI is at 6,530.06, still down 2.49%, but about 1.9% above its 6,408.82 low. Both are oscillating inside wide bands rather than travelling through them, which is the opposite of the no-retracement path this measure is built to detect.

Cross-assets remain quiet and unaligned. VIX settled at 15.85 inside a 15.61 to 16.06 range, low in absolute terms even after a 4.76% daily gain. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.72% and the 2-year near 4.26%, both marginally firmer after Monday's four-basis-point decline in the 10-year. WTI is near $85.28 and Brent near $92.28, both slightly higher as markets assess the announced expansion of US sanctions measures aimed at Iran and its trading partners, which so far has stopped short of imposed penalties. Gold is holding near $4,650 and its highest levels since mid-May. None of these are aligned with an equity trend leg.

The unresolved item remains the semiconductor complex. Monday's US session left the Nasdaq Composite down 0.76% at 25,980.19 and the S&P 500 down 0.28% at 7,652.86, while the Dow closed up 0.26%, a split driven by chip weakness rather than broad selling. Nvidia fell 2.9% in a seventh consecutive losing session, Micron fell 5.8% and Broadcom 2.6%. Delayed Finviz context, collected minutes before this assessment, is consistent with that: a latest-session semiconductor basket down about 3% on average with all seven names lower, technology the weakest sector at -1.71%, and megacaps split five higher against three lower. The same delayed feed shows NQ futures up about 0.3% and VIX futures marginally lower, which agrees with the live quotes rather than contradicting them. That feed is treated as supporting context only and is not used as evidence of live price-path structure.

Confidence is set at 86. Two independent NQ quotes agree on direction and range, live index levels are available for both major Asian markets, yields, oil and VIX are current, the shared cross-asset context is one minute old, and the day's scheduled US calendar has been verified. Stress holds at 46 for the unresolved chip-sector question and for the Wednesday stack, where Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and durable goods all print at 12:30Z and Nvidia reports after that session's cash close. The narrow danger window spans 13:30Z to 14:30Z, covering the US cash open and the 14:00Z cluster of CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and the Richmond Fed index.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 04:00Z on 24 August with Tail 11 and Stress 40 in a normal mode and held a 9 to 12 band through the remaining Asian hours. The first structural peak came at 07:00Z, where the European open produced Tail 19 and Stress 58 in a trend-down mode; it faded to 17 within an hour and to 12 by 09:00Z. The window's only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z, which mapped to WATCH, and the single peak at 14:00Z, which reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode and mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That peak decayed immediately, to 13 by 15:00Z and to single digits from 17:00Z onward as the US afternoon mean-reverted. The overnight hours since have run a 7 to 12 Tail band with Stress easing from 45 to 42 and then settling back near 45 to 47 as the Asian session repriced the chip-led US close. Confidence stayed in a 80 to 88 range throughout, dipping only around the cash-open event window. The dominant mode was normal at both ends of the window and mixed for most of the middle, with trend-down appearing only in the two European open hours and the single 14:00Z peak.
outlookSummary: The conditional path stays inside the low Tail band for all 24 hours, so every slot maps to EA_ON. It opens at 13 on the observed re-extension to a new overnight high, holds 13 through the Asian afternoon, and eases to 12 at the Japan cash close. It then lifts to 15 at 07:00Z for the European cash open, the same window that produced the prior session's first structural peak before fading it within an hour, and steps down through the European morning to a floor of 12 by 10:00Z. The series lifts to 13 at 12:00Z for the Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, reaches 17 at 13:00Z as the Case-Shiller release and the US cash open arrive, and peaks at 19 at 14:00Z for the CB Consumer Confidence, New Home Sales and Richmond Fed cluster. That is the highest conditional reading of the horizon and it still sits below the block threshold, because the day's US calendar carries no high-impact release and event presence alone is not treated as Tail evidence. The path then decays through the US afternoon to 12 by 18:00Z, lifts modestly to 13 for the power hour on repositioning into the Wednesday stack, and falls to a horizon low of 10 across the late US evening. It returns to 11 and then 12 through the Asian reopen and the following morning as Core PCE, the second GDP estimate, durable goods and the Nvidia report come into view. Stress traces the same shape from 46 down to 44 overnight and up to 55 at the 14:00Z cluster. Confidence declines steadily from 86 to 78 with distance from observed evidence.
